content:
I think it would be a good idea to not use the ∀ᵉ/∃ᵉ notation in mathlib. It is used quite rarely (about 100 occurrences), and for anyone who hasn't seen it before it looks pretty weird. (The ᵉ stands for extended, as this is the "extended binder notation".)

So, I made a linter in #44544 that detects usage of this notation, and gives a Try this: code action to replace the notation with normal binder notation. I then generated the adaptations using runSkimmer.sh, which did all of the replacements without error. The linter is off by default and is added to mathlib's linter set so that it is active in mathlib.

Do you agree with this change?
I guess once this lands, we could consider deprecating the notation entirely on the batteries side?
I think these indicate weaknesses in the core syntax and would rather try to make that more flexible instead of expanding the existing uses
The expanded version is only 1 character longer per binder, so I don't think we are losing much by doing these expansions.
